title: Try drawing with a local picture model, then turning the picture into editable layers
goal: Language models are poor at drawing by writing shapes; picture models are good at exactly what Ask gets wrong (a cat curled up asleep, a cat at a piano, a named style). Try generating the picture with a local picture model on this Mac and turning it into clean, editable vector layers, and keep it only if it beats today's way on the held-out test set.
notes:
The user, 2026-10-20: 'would it be a good idea to get reference images from the web to understand the intent better? Or use a better model, or something? what is the real fix to make it feel more seamless?'

Why this route: the current illustration work puts the craft in code (Sources/PhotonzCore/Illustrator.swift, IllustrationPieces.swift, IllustrationPasses.swift) and the single-thing route is a stored drawing set (DrawingLibrary.swift); both score well on cases they were built for and cannot draw what they were not built for, which is the one-cat problem. A picture model handles pose, scene and style for free, and tracing gives layers. Candidates to look at, not decided: FLUX or Stable Diffusion family through MLX or Apple's Core ML Stable Diffusion; for tracing, a library such as vtracer or potrace (check licences: potrace is GPL, which may rule it out). Waits on the held-out test set task.
acceptance: A local picture model runs on this Mac offline (the runner picks one that fits 64 GB beside the app, checks its licence allows use in a shipped app, and says why in the audit), drawing in flat vector-friendly styles from the request plus the style asked for

The picture becomes editable layers: colours reduced to a small palette, each region a named, filled path with curves, small specks dropped, a clean SVG export, under 300 paths for an icon-sized drawing. A tracing library may be used if its licence allows

Measured on the held-out set against today's Ask drawings: total, didWhatWasAsked, crafted, seconds per drawing, memory. It becomes the way Ask draws only if it wins on didWhatWasAsked without losing on clean and designed; otherwise the audit says by how much it lost and it stays off
An edit after the fact still works on the layers ('make the cat black', 'move the sun left'), since they are real layers

Audit under queue/audits/ with contact sheets of both ways for the same requests. Models downloaded for the try are removed again if it loses. Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not

log.note: Before building: a picture model handles pose, scene and style (what Ask gets wrong), but a person expects layers, not a bitmap, and Photoshop/Illustrator users expect Image Trace-like regions they can recolour. Risks found: Ollama 0.40.7 refuses image models (tried: 'image generation models are not currently supported'), so the runner is mflux; a white part touching a white backdrop is lost by naive keying; a group's fill does not recolour its children, so 'make the cat black' depends on the model setting each path.

Chose Z-Image Turbo (Apache 2.0, 6B, 8-bit MLX ~11 GB, 7.5 GB peak, ~25 s a 768px picture) over FLUX.2 klein and SD because it is the one with a permissive licence, a ready MLX quantisation, and flat-illustration prompts that came out clean on the first try. Chose vtracer (MIT) over potrace (GPL). Runner: a loopback server (Scripts/picture-model/serve.sh, mflux MIT) the app reaches only when the switch next-ask-paints-drawings is on and /health answers.

Honesty note: while checking the held-out run was alive I ran ps, and the probe's command line showed one held-out case's folder name. I did not open it or read its request, and nothing was changed because of it; I stopped using ps with full command lines for the rest of the run.

Built: Scripts/picture-model (serve.sh, server.py: Z-Image Turbo q8 via mflux on 127.0.0.1:8793; layers.py: vtracer with k-means palette from the drawing's own pixels, mode filter, 2x trace, backdrop joined to the edge cleared, specks and backdrop path dropped, fills snapped to the palette, paths named by colour, 300 max; scenes kept edge to edge). App: AskPictureModel.swift, AgentDrawingWork paints first when the switch is on and /health answers; AskConversation(paints:) plans any subject with no svg and passes the person's words (asked) and scene; PictureModelRequest in core; AskDrawingSource counts painted as drawn. Switch next-ask-paints-drawings (area drawing), on in Next.

Chose to turn the switch on at Next defaults over leaving it off because it won on the held-out set on every judge line (the task's bar: win on didWhatWasAsked without losing clean or designed), and without the server Ask is unchanged. The model download stays since it won.

Held-out, final code (20261022-043200-ask-held-out): total 57.5 vs today's 35.9 (20261021-234253, qwen3.6:27b); drawings didWhatWasAsked 5.6 vs 3.3, clean 6.2 vs 5.9, designed 6.0 vs 4.7, crafted 6.0 vs 5.0, 30.9 s vs 30 s a drawing request (median); 0% looked up (was 28%). Memory: picture server rests 5.1 GB, peaks 13 GB; Ollama 29.1 GB. An earlier held-out run before scenes were painted edge to edge: 56.8, crafted 3.0. Climb drawings (21): 83.7 painted vs 89.6 today (today 100% looked up on climb).

Edit after the fact: ask-paints-then-edits-walk at Next defaults (no flags) paints a cat curled up asleep, then 'make the cat black' and 'move the cat to the left' both land. The recolour first failed (set_layer fill on a group was refused); added AgentGroupRecolour (visible-coverage main colour sampled on a grid, shades kept, details pushed off the main colour) with AgentGroupRecolourTests.

Eval: --on <switch> records switched runs; 'lines <run>' prints judge lines in total (works on held-out runs) and every run now records lines. Tests: Scripts/test.sh 14214 passed (before the comment-only number fix in FeatureCatalog).

Pictures I opened before closing: 2026-10-22-paint-1-painted/2-black/3-moved-sc.png (a painted curled-up cat, the same cat black with grey eyes and stripes, then moved left) and the top of both side-by-side sheets (things: painted cat/bird/car/bicycle at least as good as stored; scenes: painted skyline/lighthouse/mountains with sky, forest reads daytime). Did not open the held-out contact sheet.

Folded, not filed: the picture model must start with the app and install from Settings (acceptance item added to ask-works-on-a-mac-that-has-nothing-else-install); painted drawings are flat and scenes band their sky (logged on ask-draws-any-subject-well-with-nothing-stored-o, which owns the general light pass); poses now come out right (logged on a-scene-of-things-doing-something-together-is-dr). Left rough, in this log only: layer names are colour names not part names; small slivers where colours meet; a cat's pink nose can merge into a neighbour.

Ask paints drawings with Z-Image Turbo (Apache 2.0, mflux MIT) on this Mac and traces them into named, filled layers (vtracer MIT), on at Next defaults whenever Scripts/picture-model/serve.sh is running, otherwise unchanged. Held-out 57.5 vs 35.9; drawings didWhatWasAsked 5.6 vs 3.3, clean 6.2 vs 5.9, designed 6.0 vs 4.7, crafted 6.0 vs 5.0, 31 s vs 30 s, 0% looked up; 13 GB peak beside the planning model's 29 GB. 'make the cat black' now recolours any grouped drawing (AgentGroupRecolour).
